title: Setup pass payload
description: The payload of a setup pass, the exact JSON bytes the control plane signed. Its members come in no set order: the pass carries the exact bytes signed, and the adapter parses those bytes. A setup pass is the browser form of the setup step: the step a person takes to set the adapter up at its source, the same step as setup in the source role of the adapter's description (description.schema.json). A setup pass is the payload in base64url without padding, a dot, and the signature in base64url without padding, at most 1024 characters with no white space; the signature is 64 bytes of Ed25519 under the control plane's server key over qory-setup-ed25519-v1, a line feed and the payload bytes. That first line is not the connect pass's (connect-pass.schema.json), so a connect pass never verifies as a setup pass, and a setup pass never verifies as a connect pass. The control plane gives a setup pass only to an instance admin, and makes it when the admin asks to set the adapter up, never when a page is shown. It sends the admin to the adapter's setup_url (adapter.schema.json) with the pass as the query parameter state. The control plane hands the admin's browser the address of setup_url carrying the pass only in its answer to the admin's request to set the adapter up, sent with Cache-Control: no-store; it never logs the pass, and never puts it in the address of any control plane page, so no Referer header from those pages carries it. The adapter reads the pass from the request, then answers with a redirect to an address of the adapter that does not carry the pass, so the pass leaves the browser's address bar and history, and the page the admin then sees holds no pass. The adapter sends that redirect with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, so the pass leaves in no Referer header, and with Cache-Control: no-store, so no cache keeps it. The adapter decodes the pass strictly, both parts as strict base64url without padding, and verifies the signature under a server key the adapter pinned at enrolment: after a server key rotation it tries each pinned key, and any one that verifies passes. It then reads the payload against this schema, with exactly the members this schema defines, checks that adapter_id is the id the adapter is enrolled as, and refuses a pass whose expires_at has passed on its clock, or is more than 15 minutes ahead of it; expires_at bounds only the pass's arrival at the adapter, not the admin's round trip at the source. The adapter checks expires_at before it checks whether the nonce was seen: a pass whose expires_at has passed on its clock, or is more than 15 minutes ahead of it, is refused and its nonce is never recorded. An adapter accepts a setup pass once: it records the nonce in one atomic check-and-insert, so before its expires_at the first browser to bring the pass wins, and a second arrival of the same pass is refused on the adapter's page. It keeps the nonce, in storage that survives a restart, until expires_at has passed on its clock. Once the adapter is set up at its source, it refuses every setup pass on its page, so only one setup completes, even when two admins each start one. Becoming set up is one atomic step, in which the adapter checks again that it is not set up before it keeps the setup, so two flows never both complete. When it accepts the pass, the adapter makes a random state value of at least 128 bits for this pass, and keeps the pass on its side, bound to the browser by a short-lived cookie it sets: HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax, Lax because the return from the source is a cross-site top-level navigation, scoped by Path to the adapter's setup routes, with Max-Age at most 900 seconds, no longer than the 15 minutes an accepted pass can have left (expires_at below), and under a name distinct from that of any cookie the control plane sets. The cookie's value is random and opaque, and maps to the accepted pass on the adapter's side; it is not the pass. The adapter runs one setup flow at a time; a valid pass that the adapter accepts later replaces an open flow, whose return is then refused. When the flow ends, of any outcome, the adapter clears the cookie, for example with Max-Age=0 on the same name and Path, so the binding serves one flow. The pass never leaves the adapter: the adapter sends the source only that state value, never the pass, and never logs the pass, in its access logs or in those of any reverse proxy in front of it: the query of the address that receives the pass is kept out of them. On the source's return, the adapter accepts the result only when the state value and the browser's cookie both match the same accepted pass. It takes the setup's result from the source itself, under what the source's return carries, and never trusts an id that the browser sends back alone. The adapter never logs, keeps or forwards a cookie it did not set: an adapter served under the control plane's origin receives the control plane's cookies. Nothing goes back to the control plane: unlike a connect pass, a setup pass has no return. Once set up at its source, the adapter sends its start-up body again at once, without setup_url (adapter.schema.json). Unlike connect passes, setup passes have no rule that each has a strictly later expires_at than the one before: the adapter compares no setup pass with another.

adapter_id.description: The adapter the pass is for, as the control plane enrolled it.

nonce.description: 128 random bits in base64url without padding, 22 characters, new for each pass.

expires_at.description: When the pass expires, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds, at most 15 minutes after the control plane issued it. The adapter refuses a pass whose expires_at has passed on its clock, or is more than 15 minutes ahead of it, and keeps the pass's nonce until expires_at has passed. It bounds only the pass's arrival at the adapter, not the admin's round trip at the source.
